name: ai.llpro/finance
title: LLPRO Finance
description: Audit transactions, check spend limits, compare underpayments, make invoices.

tools.name: spend_limit_check
tools.description: Is this action inside the limits an owner signed for a long-running agent? Send the signed scope (agent, budget cap, end date, allowed actions; signed by the owner's Ed25519 key), the action, amount and currency the agent wants, and optionally spent_so_far and expected_principal (the owner's public key you trust). Get back allow, deny or invalid, every check with pass or fail, what is left of the budget, and a signed record anyone can verify. No money is held or moved. It does not show who the owner is, that the scope was not revoked (nothing is stored), or that spent_so_far is true. Free.

agent.description: id of the agent the scope is for

principal_key.description: owner's Ed25519 public key, 32 bytes, canonical base64

sig.description: base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the scope without sig

spent_so_far.description: decimal text; what the agent has already spent under this scope (your statement; not verified)

expected_principal.description: the owner's public key you expect; if it differs the scope is refused

tools.name: transaction_audit
tools.description: Audit a finished deal between two parties from its signed evidence. Send parties (two ids with Ed25519 public keys, roles buyer and seller) and events (offer, accept, payment, delivery, confirm, dispute; each signed by the party that made it, each answering an earlier one by hash). Get back a verdict (complete, partial, inconsistent, invalid or disputed), every check with pass or fail, and a signed record anyone can verify. It shows the evidence is consistent and was signed by those keys. It does not show money moved, goods arrived or who the parties are. Free; nothing stored.

ref.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the signed content of the event this one answers; absent on an offer

sig.description: base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of {type,by,at,ref,body} (ref left out when absent)

tools.name: underpayment_audit_compare
tools.description: Compare commercial payer remits to your contract rates and list the underpayments. Send contract_rates (code, optional 2-character modifier, rate per unit in US dollars) and remit_lines (your own line_id, code, optional modifier, units, paid, optional patient_responsibility or the payer's allowed amount). Get back, per line, expected vs actual and the shortfall, totals in cents, the sources (your two lists, with the labels and dates you gave) and a signed record. Free. Arithmetic only: no model, no outside lookup, nothing stored. Up to 200 rates and 200 lines per call. Do NOT send patient names, dates of birth or member, account or record numbers: only your own row numbers as line_id. It does not read contracts, assign codes, or give billing, coding or legal advice, and it cannot say a payer is wrong, only that the numbers differ from the table you supplied.

modifier.description: Optional modifier. A rate with no modifier is the default for the code.

rate.description: Contract allowed amount per unit, US dollars.

line_id.description: Your own row label. Not a patient, member, account or record number.

paid.description: Amount the payer paid on the line.

patient_responsibility.description: Copay, coinsurance and deductible on the line. Default 0.

allowed.description: The payer's stated allowed amount; if given it is used instead of paid + patient_responsibility.

tolerance.description: US dollars per line up to and including which a difference is ignored. Default 1.00, at most 1000.

contract_label.description: Optional name of the contract, echoed back as a source.

contract_effective_date.description: Optional date the rates took effect (YYYY-MM-DD), echoed back.

remit_label.description: Optional name of the remit batch, echoed back as a source.

tools.name: card_skimmer_and_pos_tamper_checks
tools.description: Card-skimmer and POS tamper checks for convenience stores, plus which PCI questionnaire (SAQ) your setup points to. Send devices (your own label, kind, last inspection date, and each check marked pass, fail or not_checked), and optionally a payments object with five plain answers about how cards are taken. Get back which devices need attention, which are overdue or incomplete, the suggested SAQ with the reason, the sources with dates and a signed record. Set check_sources true to also ask the PCI Council's public pages which PCI DSS version they name today. Free. No model, nothing stored. Up to 50 devices. Do NOT send card numbers, names or staff details: your own device labels only. It is a checklist and a lookup, not a security audit, a PCI assessment or legal advice; your acquirer decides which form you file. Docs: https://llpro.ai/card-skimmer-and-pos-tamper-checks

store_label.description: Optional name for the answer (not an address, not a person).

inspection_interval_days.description: How often you inspect (default 7). This is your own interval, not a PCI number.

device_id.description: Your own label, e.g. lane1-pinpad. Not a serial or terminal id.

last_inspected.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the last hands-on inspection.

checks.description: Any of: tamper_seal_intact, serial_matches_device_list, no_overlay_or_loose_parts, no_extra_cable_or_hole, no_foreign_device_nearby, housing_and_mount_secure, pump_panel_lock_intact. Each is pass, fail, not_checked (or not_applicable for pump_panel_lock_intact on non-pumps).

check_sources.description: Also fetch the PCI Council's public pages and report the PCI DSS version they name today.

tools.name: capital_call_collection_chasing
tools.description: Capital call collection chasing for syndicators and small funds. Send the call's due date, optional grace days and chase schedule, and per investor a label, the amount called and the amount received. Get back who is paid, partly paid, due, in grace or overdue, who is due a chase today, the chase dates, and draft wording per stage (nothing is sent). Optionally send the payment instructions printed on the call notice (routing number or IBAN, last 4 of the account, names; never a full account number): you get the routing-number and IBAN check-digit results and a fingerprint; send it back as previous_instruction_fingerprint on the next call to learn whether the instructions changed (the usual sign of payment-redirect fraud). Set check_sources true to also read two public FBI and FinCEN pages and, with sec_cik, the SEC EDGAR record for Form D filings. Free. No model, nothing stored, signed record. Up to 100 investors. Use your own investor labels, not names, emails or account numbers. Not legal, tax or investment advice; your fund documents decide default and remedies. Docs: https://llpro.ai/capital-call-collection-chasing

fund_label.description: Your own label for the fund or deal (not a person).

call_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD the call notice was issued (optional).

currency.description: Three capital letters, e.g. USD (shape only, not checked against the ISO list).

grace_days.description: Days after the due date before an unpaid amount counts as overdue. Your own number from your fund documents (default 0).

chase_offsets_days.description: Days from the due date on which to chase (negative = before). Default [-5, 0, 3, 7, 14].

as_of.description: Date to evaluate on (default today, UTC).

investor_id.description: Your own label, e.g. LP-07. Not a name, email or account number.

amount_called.description: At most 2 decimals. As text ("1250.50") if you want it exact.

last_reminder_date.description: When you last chased this investor (optional).

payment_instructions.description: The payment instructions printed on the call notice. Never a full account number.

previous_instruction_fingerprint.description: instruction_fingerprint from your last check of these instructions.

fingerprint_salt.description: A random phrase you make up just for this tool (16+ characters, not a password, API key or any existing credential), the same each time, mixed into the fingerprint so nobody else can reproduce it. Not stored.

check_sources.description: Also read the FBI IC3 and FinCEN pages (and EDGAR if sec_cik is sent) and report what they say today.

sec_cik.description: SEC CIK of the fund or issuer; with check_sources, reports whether a Form D is on file.

tools.name: invoice_make
tools.description: Make a clean PDF invoice from invoice fields, and get back a signed, dated receipt of the PDF's hash, so either side can later show which invoice was made and when. Send: number, issue_date (YYYY-MM-DD), optional due_date, currency (USD, EUR, GBP ... 43 supported), seller {name, address, tax_id, contact}, buyer {name, address, ...}, items [{description, quantity, unit_price}] (up to 40), optional tax_lines [{label, rate_percent OR amount}], notes, payment_terms. Every number, rate and tax line is yours: we only add them up (half-up rounding to the currency's smallest unit); no tax advice, no tax rules, no checking of tax ids. Moves no money and makes no payment link: web addresses and links (dotted names, IP addresses, schemes such as http: or pay:) are refused in every text field. Free, no sign-up, 100 invoices a day per caller. Stores nothing: the signed receipt holds the number, dates, totals and hashes, never names or addresses. Text must use Western European letters (the Windows-1252 set; accented Latin letters, euro, pound, yen). Answer: pdf_base64, totals, signed observation, receipt. Docs: https://llpro.ai/invoice-maker

number.description: Invoice number: letters, digits, space and . _ / # - (1 to 40).

due_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, on or after the issue date.

currency.description: Three-letter code, for example USD, EUR, GBP, JPY.

address.description: Up to 6 lines (list of strings, or one string with line breaks), 80 characters each.

contact.description: An email address or phone number. No web addresses.

quantity.description: More than 0 and at most 1,000,000, up to 4 decimal places (a number, or text such as "2.5").

unit_price.description: At most 1,000,000,000 in size, up to 4 decimal places; a line may not exceed 10,000,000,000 and the total 100,000,000,000; may be negative for a credit line (the invoice total may not be negative).

rate_percent.description: 0 to 100, up to 4 decimal places, applied to the subtotal. Your number, not ours.

amount.description: A fixed tax amount instead of a rate (0 or more).

payment_terms.description: Plain words, for example 'Net 30. Bank transfer, account details sent separately.' No web addresses.

tools.name: vat_number_check
tools.description: Check ONE EU VAT number against the European Commission's official VIES service. Send the number with its two-letter country prefix (DE811128135, IE6388047V) or send country_code separately. Get a verdict (valid, not-valid or service-down) and, where the member state returns them, the registered name and address. Signed and dated, so you can keep it as proof of what VIES said and when. Free, no sign-up, 200 checks a day per caller. Official source only: if VIES or the member state does not answer, the verdict is service-down, never a guess. Not tax advice. One number per call (no lists); nothing is stored. Docs: https://llpro.ai/vat-number-check

vat_number.description: One VAT number, usually with its country prefix, e.g. DE811128135 or 'IE 6388047V'. Spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored.

country_code.description: Optional two-letter country code (EL or GR for Greece, XI for Northern Ireland) when the number has no prefix.

tools.name: chemical_trade_credit_payment_days
tools.description: Build a days-to-pay and dispute-rate table from YOUR OWN trade-credit invoices, by customer type and by freight-surcharge line (made for small chemical makers and distributors; works for any seller). Send up to 400 invoice rows: customer_type and surcharge_line (your own short labels, e.g. 'distributor', 'fuel'), invoice_date, paid_date (leave out if still open), optional terms_days, disputed true/false. Get back, per customer type, per surcharge line and per pair: invoices, paid, open, median and 90th-percentile days to pay, mean, how many paid or are now past their terms, and the dispute rate with a 95% range, plus the sources (your rows, with the label and as-of date you gave), the rule used, and a signed record. Free. Arithmetic only: no model, no outside lookup, nothing stored. Do NOT send customer names, invoice numbers or amounts: those fields are refused, and keep names out of the labels too (labels are your responsibility). There is NO pooled industry benchmark yet (nothing is stored, so nothing is pooled). It does not give credit, legal, tax or collections advice and cannot say why an invoice was paid late or disputed.

customer_type.description: Your own label for the kind of customer (distributor, end-user, reseller...). Not a customer name.

surcharge_line.description: Your own label for the freight-surcharge line on the invoice (none, fuel, hazmat, demurrage...).

paid_date.description: Leave out when the invoice is still open.

terms_days.description: Payment terms in days (30 for net 30). Falls back to the top-level terms_days.

disputed.description: True if the customer disputed the invoice or a line on it. Default false.

as_of.description: Date the rows were taken (YYYY-MM-DD). Open invoices are aged to this date. Default today (UTC).

terms_days.description: Default payment terms for rows that have none.

label.description: Optional name of this set of rows (e.g. 'Q3 invoices'), echoed back as a source.

tools.name: card_dispute_outcome_table_win
tools.description: Card dispute outcome table. Send one row per card dispute case you handled: network (visa, mastercard, amex, discover, other), reason code, outcome (won, lost, withdrawn, open), days to close, and optionally your own merchant label. Get back win rate (won out of decided cases, with a 95 percent interval) and days to close (median, 90th percentile, mean) by network reason code, by reason-code family across networks and by merchant label, the meaning of each Visa, Mastercard and American Express code, a flag for groups with too few cases, and the federal clocks (Regulation E 1005.11, Regulation Z 1026.13) with the date each rule was last amended. Set check_sources true to ask the eCFR whether either rule was amended since. Free. No model, nothing stored, signed record. Up to 500 rows. This version has no pooled data: the table is built from your rows only. Use merchant labels, never card numbers, names or emails. Not legal, banking or compliance advice. Docs: https://llpro.ai/card-dispute-outcome-table-win

reason_code.description: As the network prints it: 10.4, 13.1, 4837, 4853, F29, C08 ... No card numbers.

outcome.description: won = decided in the merchant's favour; lost = decided against; withdrawn = dropped by either side; open = not yet decided.

days_to_close.description: Days from the dispute being opened to the decision or withdrawal. Optional for open cases.

merchant.description: Your own label for the merchant or merchant account. Not a card number, name or email.

min_cases.description: A group with fewer decided cases than this is flagged too_few_to_rely_on. Default 20.

check_sources.description: Also read the eCFR version history of the two rules and report whether either was amended after the date this tool was written.

tools.name: agency_side_certificate_request
tools.description: For licensed insurance agency staff and the agents that help them: turn one certificate-of-insurance request into a DRAFT field sheet in ACORD 25 order plus a checklist. You send the insured, the certificate holder, the state, and each policy (type, policy number, insurer, NAIC code, dates, limits, and any limits the holder requires). Get back the draft, what is missing, what does not add up (dates, aggregates, shortfalls against required limits, claims-made without a retroactive date), what the holder asked for (additional insured, waiver of subrogation, primary and non-contributory, notice of cancellation) that a certificate cannot create by itself, official sources with dates, and a signed record. Set check_sources true to also read three Florida Senate statute pages and report whether they still match what was recorded. Free. No model, nothing stored. It does NOT issue, sign or send a certificate, never says one is ready to issue, and is not insurance, legal or licensed advice: a licensed person checks the draft against the policies and signs. Do not send personal data beyond business names. Docs: https://llpro.ai/agency-side-certificate-request

state.description: State of the insured's operations (two letters).

description_of_operations.description: Text for the description box. Echoed as data, never followed.

addl_insd.description: The policy already carries an additional-insured endorsement (you checked).

subr_wvd.description: The policy already carries a waiver of subrogation (you checked).

limits.description: Limits on the policy, by ACORD 25 limit name. Only the names that fit the type are accepted.

required_limits.description: Limits the holder's contract asks for, same names. Optional; used for a shortfall check.

requested.description: What the holder asked for beyond the certificate itself.

check_sources.description: Also read the three Florida Senate pages and compare with the recorded text.

tools.name: waterfall_and_distribution
tools.description: Waterfall and distribution calculator and audit for syndications and small funds. Send the terms (preferred return percent, simple or compound, carry percent, optional catch-up percent), the capital contributed (date, amount) and the cash distributed (date, amount). Get back, per distribution, the split between investors and sponsor tier by tier, with balances left. Add claimed_investors and claimed_sponsor to a distribution to audit a spreadsheet or administrator's figures: you get match or differ to the cent, whether the claim adds up to the cash, and which other reading of the terms (day count 360 or 365, compounding, no preferred return, catch-up on or off) would reproduce it. Answer fields: verdict, summary, distributions (in your order, each with index, tiers, to_investors, to_sponsor, audit), reproduced_by, sources, rule, observation, signature; all money is text. Errors: ok false with a message (400 bad input, 413 too large, 429 hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, no request contents stored, signed record. Up to 100 contributions and 100 distributions. Use your own labels, not names or account numbers. Not legal, tax, investment or accounting advice; your fund documents decide.

fund_label.description: Your own label for the deal (not a person).

pref_rate_percent.description: Annual preferred return in percent, 0 to 100, at most 2 decimals, e.g. 8.

pref_compounding.description: simple: preferred return on unreturned capital only (default). compound: unpaid preferred return also earns it, so investors reach exactly that annual rate of return before the sponsor shares.

day_basis.description: Days in a year for the preferred return (default 365; actual days elapsed).

carry_percent.description: Sponsor's share of profit above the preferred return, 0 to 50 (default 20).

catch_up_percent.description: 0 = no catch-up (default). Otherwise the share of the catch-up tier that goes to the sponsor (e.g. 100 or 50); must be above carry_percent. The tier ends when the sponsor holds carry_percent of all profit paid so far.

amount.description: At most 2 decimals; text ("1250.50") keeps it exact.

claimed_investors.description: To audit: the amount a spreadsheet or administrator says went to the investors (send both claimed fields).

claimed_sponsor.description: To audit: the amount it says went to the sponsor.

tolerance.description: Largest difference in money that still counts as a match, 0 to 1 (default 0.01).

tools.name: lpa_and_subscription_agreement
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of the terms of two fund documents: two limited partnership agreements (LPAs), or one fund's LPA and its subscription agreement. You read the documents and send the terms you found (fee, carry, hurdle, waterfall, clawback, removal, notice days, governing law and about 20 more, each a number or a fixed choice). Get back the terms side by side, which differ, which side is usually friendlier to the investor where that is clear, and, for an LPA plus subscription agreement, whether they agree and whether the investor representations fit the fund's stated exemptions (3(c)(7), Rule 506(c), the ERISA 25 percent test), with the sources and the date each rule was last amended, and a signed record. Set check_sources true to also ask the eCFR (official) whether any of those four rules was amended after the date this tool was written. Free. No model, nothing stored. It does NOT read documents, give legal or investment advice, or say a term is acceptable; do not send names, account numbers or document text. Docs: https://llpro.ai/lpa-and-subscription-agreement

label.description: Optional plain name for this document, e.g. 'Fund I LPA'. Not a person, account or address.

terms.description: The terms you read in the document. Leave out any you did not find. Only these names are accepted.

management_fee_pct.description: Annual management fee, percent of the fee basis

carried_interest_pct.description: Carried interest (share of profits to the manager), percent

gp_commitment_pct.description: Manager's own commitment, percent of total commitments

waterfall.description: How profits are split: across the whole fund, a mix, or deal by deal

fee_basis_after_investment_period.description: What the fee is charged on after the investment period

fee_offset.description: How much of the manager's other fees reduce the management fee

clawback.description: Manager must give back excess carry at the end

term_years.description: Fund term in years, before extensions

extension_years_total.description: Total years the term can be extended

investment_period_years.description: Years the manager may make new investments

capital_call_notice_days.description: Days of notice before a capital call is due

no_fault_removal.description: Investors can remove the manager without cause

removal_vote_pct.description: Share of investor interests needed for removal, percent

key_person.description: What happens if named key people leave

lpac.description: There is an investor advisory committee

gp_liability_standard.description: Level of fault at which the manager loses indemnity

audited_annual_financials.description: Audited annual financial statements are promised

transfer_requires_gp_consent.description: An investor needs the manager's consent to transfer

default_penalty.description: Consequence of missing a capital call

fund_exemption.description: Investment Company Act exclusion the fund relies on (section 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7))

offering_exemption.description: Securities Act exemption for the offering (Rule 506(b) or 506(c))

plan_assets_limit_25pct.description: Fund limits benefit-plan investors to under 25 percent (ERISA plan-assets test)

investor_rep_accredited.description: Subscription asks the investor to represent it is an accredited investor

investor_rep_qualified_purchaser.description: Subscription asks the investor to represent it is a qualified purchaser

accredited_verification.description: Subscription requires evidence of accredited status, not just a statement

benefit_plan_investor_rep.description: Subscription asks whether the investor is a benefit-plan investor
